In [[mathematics]], precisely in the [[Function of several complex variables|theory of functions of several complex variables]], a '''pluriharmonic function''' is a [[real number|real valued]] [[Function (mathematics)|function]] which is [[Local property|locally]] the [[real part]] of a holomorphic function of several complex variables. Sometimes  such a function is referred to as '''''n''-harmonic function''', where ''n'' ≥ 2 is the [[Dimension (mathematics)|dimension]] of the [[Domain (mathematical analysis)|complex domain]] where the function is defined.<ref>See for example {{harv|Severi|1958|p=196}} and {{harv|Rizza|1955|p=202}}. {{harvtxt|Poincaré|1899|pp=111–112}} calls such functions "''fonctions biharmoniques''", irrespective of the [[Dimension (mathematics)|dimension]] ''n'' ≥ 2 : his paper is perhaps{{cn|date=February 2020}} the older one in which the [[pluriharmonic operator]] is expressed using the first order [[partial differential operator]]s now called [[Wirtinger derivatives]].</ref> However, in modern expositions of the theory of functions of several complex variables<ref>See for example the popular textbook by {{harvtxt|Krantz|1992|p=92}} and the advanced (even if a little outdated) [[monograph]] by {{harvtxt|Gunning|Rossi|1965|p=271}}.</ref> it is preferred to give an equivalent formulation of the concept, by defining pluriharmonic function a [[complex number|complex valued]] function whose restriction to every complex [[Line (geometry)|line]] is a [[harmonic function]] with respect to the [[real part|real]] and [[imaginary part]] of the complex line parameter.

==Formal definition==
{{EquationRef|1|Definition 1}}. Let {{math|''G'' ⊆ '''C'''{{sup|''n''}}}} be a [[Domain (mathematical analysis)|complex domain]] and {{math|''f'' : ''G'' → '''R'''}} be a {{math|''C''{{i sup|2}}}} (twice [[Differentiable function|continuously differentiable]]) function. The function {{math|''f''}} is called '''pluriharmonic''' if, for every [[Complex number|complex]] [[Line (geometry)|line]]

:<math>\{ a + b z \mid z \in \Complex \} \subset \Complex^n</math>

formed by using every couple of complex [[tuple]]s {{math|''a'', ''b'' ∈ '''C'''{{sup|''n''}}}}, the function

:<math>z \mapsto f(a + bz)</math>

is a [[harmonic function]] on the set

:<math>\{ z \in \Complex \mid a + b z \in G \} \subset \Complex .</math>


{{EquationRef|2|Definition 2}}. Let {{math|''M''}} be a [[complex manifold]] and {{math|''f'' : ''M'' → '''R'''}} be a {{math|''C''{{i sup|2}}}} function. The function {{math|''f''}} is called '''pluriharmonic''' if
:<math>dd^c f = 0.</math>

==Basic properties==
Every pluriharmonic function is a [[harmonic function]], but not the other way around. Further, it can be shown that for [[holomorphic function]]s of several complex variables the real (and the imaginary) parts are locally pluriharmonic functions. However a function being harmonic in each variable separately does not imply that it is pluriharmonic.
